hypothesis: Question: does any demographic or voice signal transfer to unseen patients beyond the train median, and if so, which feature subset and weighting carries it? Prior evidence (development, 7 held-out patients, row RMSE): median 8.379 < standardized Ridge(alpha=10) 8.523 < HGB(250 iter) 10.465, group MAE ordered the same way. This ordering is consistent with the competing explanation that row-level fits mostly learn patient-specific structure (rows are correlated within patient; motor_UPDRS variance is largely between-patient) that does not transfer, rather than with 'features are pure noise'. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: (A) if transferable signal exists, some heavily regularized ridge (alpha >=100), possibly demographics-only or log-transformed jitter/shimmer/NHR, or equal-patient sample weighting, will beat the median in 7-fold GroupKFold CV over the 28 train patients and also on development; (B) if no signal transfers, GroupKFold CV will select the median (or near-median shrinkage) and the development loss will be ~8.38, which would be a useful negative result pointing away from feature-based row regression toward other representations. The program selects by group-CV RMSE only on train, refits on all train, clips predictions to the train y range, and reports per-candidate CV RMSE/equal-patient MAE, the best candidate per feature-set/weighting, and 28-patient-level correlations between per-patient mean features and mean motor_UPDRS as diagnostics. No transductive use of unlabeled inputs; standardization and log floors come from train only. A narrow fallback to the train median is reported explicitly in findings if it ever triggers. This is exploratory; joint changes (feature set, transform, weighting, alpha) mean the development score alone does not attribute gains to one factor, but the CV table separates them internally.
